newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Schmidhuber says EMU to start on time.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Schmidhuber says EMU to start on time.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Peter Schmidhuber said on Thursday that he expected European monetary union (EMU) would start as scheduled on January 1, 1999 and that any considerations about a delay were not an issue at present.
Speaking to reporters ahead of a conference of economic ministers, Schmidhuber said, "I expect that the date of January 1, 1999 will be kept."

Asked if he thought a delay would require a renegoiation of the Maastricht Treaty, Schmidhuber said, "I do not regard such considerations as being an issue at present because I expect monetary union to start on time."

Asked if he was concerned that the German government may be departing from its stance of strict adherence to the Maastricht criteria, Schmidhuber said that Finance Minister Theo Waigel had only last Monday underlined that the government would do all it could to meet the criteria exactly.
